findings.description: The spec does not define what enabling post-processing does when the OS refuses one of its shortcuts. The branch now refuses to enable post-processing in that case, which changes today's toggle behavior; because the post-processing shortcut editor is only reachable once post-processing is enabled, the user can be locked out of fixing the refused shortcut from the UI. The spec only says the disabled state behaves 'as today' and that legacy shortcuts keep their behavior.
findings.suggestion: Decide in Clarify. Recommended: enabling post-processing always succeeds as today; a refused shortcut is reported (toast and row warning, like inherited conflicts) and can be edited; OS refusal stays a rejection only for shortcut additions and changes (AC-004).
